A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete text, algorithms, equations, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched despite renaming and substantial experimental reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-selection experiments using real text-to-image generators and synthetic image, captioning and video tasks, plus hyperparameter studies.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and reports additional model comparisons, adaptation experiments, sensitivity studies and execution-time measurements.

M1.justification: SCK-UCB is renamed PAK-UCB. Algorithms 2–4 retain the same per-arm kernel regression, optimistic selection, RFF approximation and staged theoretical variant. Expanded explanations and new evaluation scenarios do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: The MS-COCO and MSR-VTT generation tasks remain, including the synthetic experiments moved into Appendix D. V2 adds dedicated train/baseball-bat and elephant/fire-hydrant prompt categories and scenarios where generators or prompt categories arrive during operation, substantially extending the earlier stationary coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds actual plotted comparisons against LinUCB, KernelUCB-poly3 and One-arm Oracle, including in retained experiments such as Figure 2 and the synthetic tasks. Naive-KRR remains, and PAK-UCB-lin matches the earlier SCK-UCB-lin rather than constituting a new comparator.

E3.justification: New protocols introduce UniDiffuser after 2,500 iterations and additional prompt categories every 1,000 iterations. V1's four-generator static test is absent; v2 includes a three-generator carrot/bowl test. Reporting narrows from O2B, OPR and 100-iteration moving-average OPR to the first two metrics.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining the RFF bandwidth and feature-count studies, v2 adds tests of adaptation to arriving models/categories, polynomial-kernel scale sensitivity, KRR regularization sensitivity and measured computational efficiency (Figures 4 and 11–17). These address substantial additional robustness and practical-efficiency questions.

E5.justification: Both versions report curves averaged over 20 trials and use ± values for illustrative mean CLIPScores. V2 follows the same reporting practice without adding seed information, defined confidence intervals, significance tests or an increased repeated-run count.

E6.justification: V2 adds results for new generator pairs, baselines, adaptation and sensitivity tests, plus approximately 10 versus under 2 minutes for 2,000 iterations in Figure 17. V1's four-generator and moving-average OPR results disappear. Adaptation results have an internal inconsistency: Figures 11–12 duplicate curves, and Figure 11(a) differs from Figure 4(a).

T1.justification: The assumptions, regret bounds, RFF approximation bounds and proofs remain substantively unchanged. V1 Appendices B–D match v2 Appendices A–C. Restating the existing lower-bound quantity c in the variance proof and correcting notation do not introduce new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The model-selection objective, kernel/RFF contributions and regret claims remain. V2 extends the introduction's empirical superiority claim from greedy baselines to standard LinUCB and KernelUCB, and more explicitly presents per-arm prediction as addressing their shared reward-model restriction.

C2.justification: V2 expands the explanation of arm-specific reward functions and interprets beating One-arm Oracle as outperforming a user who knows the best single model. Section 6.2 also emphasizes nonlinear kernels. V1's blanket kernel-approximation motivation is removed; the proposed future extensions to language models and other quality criteria remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies eta=1 alongside the retained alpha=1, adds UniDiffuser access information and reports execution times. Existing CLIP features, cached RFFs and default feature counts remain. However, Section 6's unscaled polynomial kernel conflicts with Appendix D's retained gamma=5, leaving its experimental scale ambiguous.

R1.justification: V2 more explicitly positions per-arm prediction against the shared-weight formulation of prior linear and kernelized contextual bandits. The related-work survey remains largely intact. Bao et al. (2023) is added, while the Lin et al. MS-COCO reference is removed despite continued dataset use.

P1.justification: V2 revises the method explanations and terminology throughout, restructures Section 6 into experimental details, summary and setups, and moves the synthetic experiments into an expanded Appendix D. The former proof appendices B–D become A–C. This substantially changes the experimental narrative and document organization.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a two-example overview, with the earlier detailed example retained as Figure 5. Experimental plots are broadly redrawn from three panels to two, with expanded legends and numerous added displays; synthetic illustrations are relocated. Figures 11 and 12 incorrectly reuse identical plots under different scenario captions.

improvement.justification: V1 lacked direct experimental comparisons with standard contextual-bandit algorithms. V2 adds these controls across real and synthetic tasks and broadens the real-generator comparisons, substantially strengthening evidence for the proposed approach's usefulness. New sensitivity and timing results further support its practical claims. Duplicated adaptation plots and conflicting polynomial-kernel disclosures weaken portions of the added evidence, but the central comparative-validation gains remain substantial.
